lead: >-
  Los Penitentes lies on the high-mountain road from Mendoza toward Aconcagua and the Chilean border. An active 13-day Ada Tours itinerary through Argentina visits this area: on day 4, travelers head into the Andes, stop near the ski resort village, and continue toward the Inca Bridge, Aconcagua, and Las Cuevas. This is a stop on a scenic mountain excursion, not a promise of skiing. Discover how Los Penitentes fits into a longer journey, how an independent mountain excursion differs from a tour, and what weather conditions to consider along the road.
---

## Tours through Los Penitentes: choosing a trip to the Andes

[Los Penitentes](/argentina/place/los-penitentes/) lies in the Argentine Andes, on the road from [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) to the Chilean border. For travelers, it is an opportunity to see a high-altitude valley, rocky ridges, and a historic ski area on the way to other natural attractions. It is convenient to visit as part of the "High Andes" route, which makes several stops along National Route 7.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Los Penitentes **on the main itinerary**. Its presence in a tour's geography means a stop or visit specified in the program. It does not in itself confirm operating ski lifts, equipment rentals, or included skiing.

The main question is straightforward: would you prefer **one day of Andean scenery** within a longer Argentina journey or a standalone excursion from Mendoza? These formats differ in duration, geography, and included services.

## An active multi-day itinerary via Los Penitentes

On the [13-day Buenos Aires, Mendoza, San Juan, and Puerto Madryn tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/), the mountains occupy a particular part of the itinerary rather than the entire trip. After exploring [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), travelers fly to Mendoza. **Day 4** is devoted to an excursion into the Andes, returning to the hotel in the evening.

The route first reaches [Uspallata](/argentina/place/uspallata/), then passes through Los Penitentes. Following a stop, the journey continues to the natural [Inca Bridge (Puente del Inca)](/argentina/place/puente-del-inca/), the [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) area, and the highland village of [Las Cuevas](/argentina/place/las-cuevas/). A walk in the Aconcagua park area and photo stops are included in the description; a technical summit ascent is not part of this program.

The itinerary then changes direction. The [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/) offers winery visits, followed by [San Juan](/argentina/place/san-juan/) and the Patagonian leg around [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) and the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/). This route suits travelers hoping to discover cities, wine culture, the Andes, and the Atlantic coast's wildlife on one trip. Los Penitentes is just one stop on a full mountain day.

### What exactly is included on the mountain day?

The excursion starts after breakfast, lasts **a full day**, and ends back in Mendoza. At Los Penitentes, the itinerary specifies passing through the ski resort area on the way to the Inca Bridge and Aconcagua. It does not promise downhill skiing, snowboarding, or a paid cable-car ascent.

This distinction is particularly important in winter: snow can make the landscape attractive, but road access and the operation of tourist facilities depend on actual conditions. If skiing is your objective, confirm it separately rather than assume it is available from the name of the former ski center.

## A separate excursion from Mendoza: what's different?

Our catalog also includes a standalone [mountain excursion from Mendoza to Aconcagua and the Inca Bridge](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-aconcagua-puente-del-inca-tour/). This is a **6-hour group program** with an English-speaking guide. Its description covers mountain areas, Uspallata, Los Penitentes, the Inca Bridge, and views of Aconcagua. It has its own terms, price, and list of included services.

This excursion suits visitors already staying in Mendoza who want to devote part of their trip to the mountains. The 13-day tour, by contrast, links the mountain day with several regions of Argentina, accommodation, and travel in a longer program. The existence of a separate excursion on the site does not mean that its group format is automatically included in the multi-day tour price. Refer to the terms of the specific product.

| Format | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [13-day tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/) | Los Penitentes within the mountain day of a larger route |
| [6-hour excursion](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-aconcagua-puente-del-inca-tour/) | Separate group trip from Mendoza |

If you plan several days in the area, compare these options with other [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/). The day's itinerary matters more than a list of place names: the same geographical direction can mean very different amounts of time for walking.

## What can you see on the road to Los Penitentes?

The mountain journey starts beyond Mendoza's green streets. As the road climbs toward the Andes, the landscape changes: vineyards and valleys recede, giving way to dry slopes, winding roads, and increasingly high mountains. Some sections feature remnants of older transport infrastructure, recalling the longstanding connection between Argentina and Chile through this corridor.

[Uspallata](/argentina/place/uspallata/) makes a convenient first stop in the mountains. Farther along lies Los Penitentes, with its characteristic rock formations. Beyond it is [Puente del Inca](/argentina/place/puente-del-inca/), with a natural stone arch and mineral deposits. Another major highlight is [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/), South America's highest peak. At [Las Cuevas](/argentina/place/las-cuevas/), the road approaches the Chilean border.

All these sites share a transport corridor but have different visiting conditions. Stopping at Los Penitentes is not the same as entering Aconcagua Park; a viewpoint near the Inca Bridge does not entail walking across the natural arch itself. On a long mountain day, setting priorities in advance helps ensure photo stops do not crowd out key visits.

## Seasons, roads, and preparation

For a scenic trip to Los Penitentes, mountain visibility and the condition of international Route 7 matter. In colder months, high-altitude stretches may experience snow, ice, strong winds, and temporary traffic restrictions. Argentine border authorities repeatedly reported precautionary closures of the Cristo Redentor corridor in 2026. That does not mean the road is permanently shut: conditions change with the weather and road authority decisions.

Check the latest official road reports before heading into the Andes. Even if you will not cross into Chile, restrictions on higher sections can alter the order of stops. In winter, bring warm clothes, wind protection, and shoes suited to cold or wet ground. Sun protection is also needed in the mountains on clear days.

Los Penitentes is historically known for its ski facilities, but recreational services depend on the season and permitted operations. A sightseeing tour is built around the mountain drive itself; skiing, lifts, and snow activities should not be assumed to be included unless specifically stated in the chosen program.

## Who should choose a route via Los Penitentes?

For first-time visitors to Argentina who want to see the Andes, a program with several distinct natural stops is convenient. On the [13-day journey](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/), the mountain section complements city walks, wineries, and the Patagonian coast. It is a choice for travelers who appreciate variety rather than a trip devoted solely to high-altitude trekking.

If you have already arranged a stay in Mendoza, consider the [standalone mountain excursion](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-aconcagua-puente-del-inca-tour/) and its duration, group format, and stated route. A serious ascent of Aconcagua requires a very different timetable, preparation, and program: a scenic roadside stop is not a mountaineering expedition.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Los Penitentes

### Does Ada Tours have a tour that actually passes through Los Penitentes?

Yes. On the [13-day Argentina tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/), Los Penitentes is listed on day 4, on the mountain route from Mendoza. The excursion continues to the Inca Bridge, Aconcagua, and Las Cuevas.

### Is skiing included?

The published description of the mountain day does not include skiing or snowboarding. Los Penitentes is a sightseeing stop. Ski services must be checked separately for the relevant season.

### How much time is spent at Los Penitentes?

On the multi-day tour, it is part of **one full day** in the Andes, rather than an overnight stay at the ski resort. Time is shared among Uspallata, Los Penitentes, the Inca Bridge, Aconcagua area, and Las Cuevas.

### Can I go there only on an excursion from Mendoza?

Yes, the website offers a separate [6-hour group mountain excursion](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-aconcagua-puente-del-inca-tour/). Its format and conditions differ from the multi-day tour.

### Why is the weather so important?

Los Penitentes is in a high-altitude transport corridor. Snow and strong winds can restrict traffic, so the visit depends on actual road conditions. Check the latest road and border authority notices before leaving.

### How is this different from climbing Aconcagua?

A sightseeing excursion shows mountain valleys and accessible visitor sites in one day. Reaching the summit requires a separate program, acclimatization, and specialist preparation. The mere presence of [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) on a route does not mean an attempt to climb it.

## Luján de Cuyo: Malbec wineries at the foot of the Andes

Luján de Cuyo is a wine-producing district of Mendoza Province in western [Argentina](/argentina/). Vineyards sit alongside avenues of poplar trees, backed by the Andes. The area is best known for red Malbec wines, but it also offers travelers the chance to compare small estates, large wineries, and restaurants set among the vines.

The journey is easy to begin in [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/). For a single outing, choose wineries with their distances, visit formats, and reservation requirements in mind. A tasting and a full lunch with wine pairing require different amounts of time.

## Agrelo, Vistalba, and Chacras de Coria: where to go

Luján de Cuyo includes several areas with different visitor experiences.

| Area | Reason to visit |
|---|---|
| Agrelo | Vineyards and large estates |
| Vistalba | Wine and foothill views |
| Chacras de Coria | Restaurants, small hotels, and walks |
| Las Compuertas | Wine-growing scenery and tastings |

**Agrelo**, south of Mendoza, is known for wineries working with red grape varieties. When selecting an estate, compare more than brand recognition: some visits showcase vineyards and production, some focus on barrel aging, and others primarily offer tastings.

**Vistalba** is attractive for a trip with views of the foothills. **Chacras de Coria** fits a more relaxed day with a walk and restaurant. Administrative boundaries are of little use when planning, however: actual driving time between wineries matters more than whether they belong to the same department.

## Planning a wine day

A winery may offer a production tour, vineyard walk, tasting flight, wine-paired lunch, or special meeting with an estate representative. Verify the actual package: a restaurant on the property does not necessarily mean lunch is included in the excursion.

For a relaxed day, choose **two different wineries**, or one extended visit with lunch. Trying to visit four distant estates often turns the experience into a succession of drives and waiting periods. Confirm the tour language and provisions for guests who do not drink alcohol.

Travelers who want to compare local wines and regional cuisine can explore [Argentina food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/). Our [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/) also offers broader journeys where Mendoza is only one stop.

## Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley: what's the difference?

Both belong to Mendoza's wine geography, but outings differ in distance and landscape. Luján de Cuyo is easier to use for a tasting day from Mendoza city. The Uco Valley lies farther south, with different vineyard scenery against the high Andes, so it often deserves a separate outing.

If you want to understand terroir differences, visit one or two estates in each area on different days. Rushing through both regions in one day generally leaves too little time to talk to winemakers, taste wines, and eat. Confirm the actual addresses of selected wineries: large regional labels on a map cannot replace a route between them.

## When to travel and what to consider

The grape harvest takes place in late summer and early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere. Visitors may see wineries at work, but harvest dates depend on grape varieties and the year. Other seasons are interesting too: cellars and tasting rooms keep their own schedules, which should be checked in advance.

The sun can be strong in Mendoza's dry climate, so a hat and water are useful for daytime walks. Arrange a driver or transport for winery visits, especially if several tastings are planned. Some estates accept visitors only by reservation, while others offer separate tariffs and extended food experiences.

Luján de Cuyo is also connected to the mountain areas of Potrerillos and the thermal destination of Cacheuta. However, winery visits and mountain outings are better treated as separate activities with different durations. You can combine them on one journey through Mendoza without promising to fit both into the same day.

## Frequently asked questions about Luján de Cuyo

### Can you visit wineries without a car?

Yes, with a prearranged transfer or excursion. This is more convenient than driving yourself for a tasting program. Agree the transport route and included visits in advance.

### How is Luján de Cuyo different from Mendoza?

Mendoza is the city and departure point for travel. Luján de Cuyo is a neighboring department with vineyards, wine districts, and its own gastronomic facilities.

### Should tastings be booked in advance?

Yes, particularly if you want to meet a particular winemaker, take a tour in a certain language, or eat at a winery restaurant. Walk-in availability should not be assumed.

## Tours through Luján de Cuyo: choosing a winery itinerary

[Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/) lies in the [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) wine region of western Argentina. It is famous for Malbec, vineyards with Andean views, and estates that introduce guests to winemaking. **The number and content of wine-focused days matter most when choosing a tour:** an itinerary might offer one tasting, 3 wineries in a day, or several different wine regions.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Luján de Cuyo among the places listed in the itinerary. The programs are not identical. We have distinguished day-by-day confirmed visits from cases where the general list of destinations is broader than the excursions actually specified.

Luján de Cuyo has a wine designation called Denominación de Origen Controlada (DOC). It is primarily associated with Malbec and regulates the origin and characteristics of wines participating in the system. However, a tasting at any winery in the area does not automatically mean every wine served has DOC designation.

## Which tours dedicate a day to Luján de Cuyo?

### 15 days: Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley on separate days

On the [private Argentina: From Iguazú to Patagonia journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/), **day 10** is devoted to Luján de Cuyo. The program lists a winery visit and tasting with a Russian-speaking guide. The following day focuses on the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/). In 2 days, travelers can experience different wine-growing areas, while other days are devoted to Iguazú, northern Argentina, and Perito Moreno Glacier.

### 17 days: 3 wineries and lunch overlooking the Andes

On the [17-day Chile and Argentina Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), **day 12** includes 3 wineries in Luján de Cuyo, with tours, tastings, and lunch overlooking the Andes at the third estate. The specific wineries are arranged in advance. Before the wine day, guests explore different parts of Chile and Patagonia; afterward, they head toward Iguazú and Buenos Aires. This is a full wine-focused stop within a wide-ranging itinerary.

### 26 days: a day in the Luján Valley followed by the Uco Valley

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) arrives in Mendoza before **day 12, with visits to 3 wineries in the Luján Valley** and tastings. Day 13 is reserved for the Uco Valley. This tour suits travelers who want to combine wineries, northern Argentina, Iguazú, the lake district of Patagonia, and southern nature routes in a single extended journey.

### Two other programs: check the actual days

The [15-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-patagonia-highlights-2024/) includes an outing to Luján de Cuyo with a wine guide and visits to 2–3 wineries. The named estates are options, not a final confirmed list.

The [9-day Argentina–Chile wine tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) is also associated with Luján de Cuyo in the catalog, but **its detailed wine day is devoted to the Uco Valley**, followed by a visit to the Chilean winery Concha y Toro. Therefore, a separate visit specifically to Luján de Cuyo is not guaranteed on this tour. If Malbec from a particular valley is important to you, compare the itinerary day by day.

| Program | Key wine-day details |
|---|---|
| [15 days: Iguazú and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) | Luján de Cuyo, then Uco |
| [17 days: Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) | 3 wineries and lunch |
| [26 days: Grand Argentina](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) | 3 wineries, then Uco |
| [9 days: wine tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) | The detailed program specifies Uco |

## Luján de Cuyo versus the Uco Valley: what changes for travelers?

Both areas are part of Mendoza's wine geography, but **they are two distinct places to visit**. Luján de Cuyo is famous for historic estates and Malbec; the Uco Valley is in a different part of the Andean foothills. Even if wine is the common theme, the visits, specific wineries, and travel between them differ.

For one day, choose several wineries within a single area and leave time for tastings, production tours, and lunch if included. With 2 wine days, divide them between Luján de Cuyo and Uco, as on the [15-day](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) and [26-day](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) programs.

Standalone options are also available in the region: [Luján de Cuyo: 3 Wineries and Lunch](/argentina/mendoza/argentina-lujan-three-wineries-lunch/), [Luján de Cuyo Winery and Tasting](/argentina/lujan-de-cuyo/lujan-de-cuyo-winery-tasting/), and [Mendoza Wineries](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-wineries-wine-tasting/). **The fact that an excursion exists separately on the website does not mean it is included in the price of every multi-day tour.**

## Combining the wine valley with an Argentina journey

Mendoza is often the main logistics base for wine visits, providing a place to stay before traveling through the vineyards. Decide in advance whether you want only the wine region or also the city, Andean foothills, and neighboring areas.

On itineraries covering several regions, arrival time in Mendoza and the date of the next flight matter. Tight flight schedules leave less room for relaxed winery visits. Compare actual tasting days, whether a guide is included, the number of estates, lunch, and what is explicitly covered by the price.

If wine is the main reason for your trip, see [Argentina food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/). If you want to combine tastings with the mountains, consider separate excursions in the Mendoza region. [Climbing Aconcagua](/argentina/tour/aconcagua-climb/) is a different travel format and requires specific physical preparation.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Luján de Cuyo

### Which itinerary includes 3 wineries and lunch?

The [17-day Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) includes 3 wineries and lunch with Andean views on day 12. The exact estates are agreed before travel.

### Can one trip include both Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley?

Yes. The [15-day journey from Iguazú to Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) and the [26-day journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) allocate separate consecutive days to the two areas.

### Does every tour that visits Mendoza include Luján de Cuyo?

No. Mendoza is a broader wine region. For example, the detailed program of the [9-day Argentina–Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) visits the Uco Valley, despite the catalog's association with Luján de Cuyo.

### Do you need a long tour just for wine tasting?

No. You can choose a standalone [Mendoza winery excursion](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-wineries-wine-tasting/), while longer tours combine a wine day with historic cities and natural areas elsewhere in Argentina.

  Martillo Island in the Beagle Channel is known for its seasonal penguin colony. Excursions depart from the Ushuaia area: some observe the birds from a boat, while others provide an authorized landing and a guided walk. Your choice depends on season, weather, and the specific program format.

## Martillo Island: when and how to see penguins near Ushuaia

**Martillo Island is a seasonal penguin-watching destination in the Beagle Channel**, east of [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/). It is often called the penguin island or *pingüinera*. For many travelers, this is the main nature attraction of a boat trip in Tierra del Fuego.

The Ushuaia tourism authority reports that penguin colonies are particularly visible **from October to April**, when the birds spend their breeding season on the island. Magellanic penguins are most common, with a smaller gentoo penguin population. Exact bird numbers, colony positions, and the possibility of landing depend on natural conditions and visitor rules.

## Which penguins live on the island?

**Magellanic penguins** have distinctive black-and-white plumage and generally nest in coastal areas. **Gentoo penguins** are recognizable by their bright orange-red bills and white head markings. Both species may be seen on one trip, although their populations on the island differ.

Penguins are wild animals. No one can guarantee that they will come close to a vessel or be at a particular stretch of shoreline when you arrive. Observe them from a safe distance and follow your guide's instructions without disturbing the birds.

The local tourism authority also mentions occasional sightings of other species, but **the main purpose of the excursion is to see Magellanic and gentoo penguins**, not to promise a rare bird encounter.

## Boat viewing or an island walk?

Travelers have two substantially different options.

| Format | Visitor experience |
|---|---|
| Watching from the water | Penguins along the shore |
| Authorized landing | Guided walk |
| Extended cruise | Other islands and sights |

**Watching from the water** allows visitors to approach the coastline along an approved boat route, but it does not grant permission to land. **Guided walks ashore** are offered only by certain operators and must comply with conservation rules. When booking, check this distinction: "penguin colony," "Martillo Island," and "walking among penguins" can refer to different services.

The trip may start at Ushuaia's port or include a road transfer to a departure point farther east, for example toward Estancia Harberton. That affects duration, stops, and the share of time spent on the water. Some excursions also visit other islands in the channel and observe seabirds and the coastline.

## Best season and the influence of weather

The main season is **October–April**. Outside breeding season, colony visits may be unavailable or less rewarding; do not assume a summer program can be operated in winter.

Wind and waves in the Beagle Channel may change boat schedules. Even in the middle of the season, captains and operators make safety-based decisions. If penguins are a priority, leave some flexibility in your itinerary instead of arranging a boat trip immediately before a tight flight connection.

Bring windproof and waterproof clothing, a warm layer, closed shoes, and protection for your camera. On the island, visitors cannot choose arbitrary photography spots or approach birds beyond the approved path.

## How does Martillo differ from Tierra del Fuego National Park?

[Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) features forests, peatlands, lakes, and walking trails on land. [Martillo Island](/argentina/place/martillo-island/) involves a sea voyage to a seasonal bird colony. The experiences complement one another, but a national park trip **does not automatically include the penguin island**.

If you have only one full day in [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), you may need to choose between a longer land-based nature excursion and a boat trip, or compare their schedules carefully. With several nights in town, combining both is easier when the weather cooperates.

## Which Ada Tours programs feature Martillo?

On the [Best of Argentina program](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), the main nature day visits Tierra del Fuego National Park, while a penguin excursion can be booked separately.

This matters when planning: **an island appearing in a trip's list of places does not automatically mean the boat excursion is paid for**. Read the sections on inclusions, extra costs, seasonal dates, and the type of landing.

## Frequently asked questions about Martillo Island

### When can you see penguins on Martillo?

The main viewing season runs approximately from October to April. Check excursion dates and availability of your chosen format with the operator.

### Can visitors land freely on the island?

No. Landings are regulated and available only on approved excursions. Many boat trips observe the penguins from the vessel.

### Can you combine Martillo and the national park in one day?

That depends on the duration of both excursions, departure times, and weather. For a relaxed itinerary, it is wiser to assign separate time slots or different days.

### Are sightings of both penguin species guaranteed?

No. Magellanic and gentoo penguins live around the island, but their numbers and positions vary.

## Which tours allow you to add Martillo Island?

**[Martillo Island](/argentina/place/martillo-island/) is an optional destination on programs staying in [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), not a required stop on every Patagonia tour.** The island lies in the [Beagle Channel](/argentina/place/beagle-channel/), and visitors come to see its colonies of Magellanic and gentoo penguins.

Our selection includes journeys with Ushuaia or other parts of southern Argentina where Martillo can be added. For example, the [12-day Ice, Sun and the End of the World tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) offers a separately paid penguin excursion. The [14-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) also lists Martillo as an optional activity. On the [11-day Argentina VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/luxury-argentina-buenos-aires-patagonia-iguazu-11-days-2026-2027/), an extra boat trip is among the options for a day in Ushuaia.

In every case, first check when you will be in Ushuaia, available free time, and the exact type of outing. **The option to visit the island does not mean a ticket is included or that a landing is guaranteed.**

## Two different ways to see the penguins

The [Martillo Island boat trip](/argentina/ushuaia/martillo-island-penguin-boat-trip/) leaves from the Ushuaia area and travels through the Beagle Channel. Birds may be observed from aboard the vessel, with the actual stops depending on the operator's program. This option involves less walking ashore, though sea travel is still subject to weather restrictions.

The [walk near the penguins](/argentina/martillo-island/martillo-penguin-walk/) is a different excursion. When a landing is authorized, participants follow a designated route accompanied by an approved guide. **Tickets for a boat trip and for a shore landing are not interchangeable.** A ship approaching the coast does not imply that passengers may go ashore.

The official Ushuaia tourism service describes several formats: departure from the city port, transfer to Puerto Almanza, or a route via Estancia Harberton. Their durations, sailing itineraries, and walking opportunities differ. When adding the experience to a main tour, choose the exact product rather than the generic description "Ushuaia penguins."

## How does Martillo fit with the main program?

A typical Ushuaia itinerary often visits [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), with Tierra del Fuego's forests, bays, and mountains. Martillo requires a separate boat trip; the transfer to the pier and sailing occupy a significant part of the day.

On the [12-day Ice, Sun and the End of the World tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/), an optional group excursion to Martillo costs **$300 per person**, paid separately. On the [14-day tour with Ushuaia and Bariloche](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), the optional excursion costs **$450 per person**. These prices belong to the respective programs and cannot automatically be transferred from one tour to another.

If you have an afternoon flight, a full sea excursion may not fit the schedule. It is better to plan Martillo for a day without a tight connection and allow room to adjust for wind and waves.

## Which season is best for the excursion?

The Ushuaia tourism portal identifies the penguin-watching season on Martillo as **approximately October to April**. Magellanic and gentoo penguins visit the island during the breeding season. Sightings of individual birds outside those months are not equivalent to the seasonal colony excursion.

For a specific date, check whether the route is operating, the restrictions on landings, and the weather. Visitors must not feed or disturb birds or approach closer than the permitted distance.

## Choosing a tour with an optional Martillo visit

If seeing penguins is the main goal, choose a program with adequate time in Ushuaia and a separately confirmed sea excursion. If you are more interested in glaciers, mountains, and waterfalls, Martillo can remain an optional addition, bearing in mind that shorter itineraries have little flexibility for weather delays.

Compare [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/), [Argentina wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/), and the [Martillo Island page](/argentina/place/martillo-island/). They support different kinds of planning, from the country's overall geography to one specific optional excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about a visit to Martillo Island

### Is Martillo Island included in the base tour price?

On the programs listed, it is an optional excursion. Read the cost and inclusions for the specific tour; an Ushuaia stop alone does not include an island visit.

### Can you land near the penguins on any boat trip?

No. Some trips only allow observation from the boat, while others include authorized shore visits. A landing is possible only on the corresponding approved excursion.

### Can you see penguins in winter?

The main excursion season follows the breeding colony's presence, approximately October to April. Do not assume a winter trip includes a colony visit without a confirmed seasonal program.

### Does Martillo replace Tierra del Fuego National Park?

No. [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) features landscapes, forests, and coastline. Martillo adds a sea outing and penguin watching.
